doc: Fable ruling ids that may stand in for a human Slack id in intercom-verify-request.sh --approved-by, and the ONLY
template classes each one authorizes. The gate and the ledger's audit-stamps read this file; nothing else does. Fail
closed: an id that is not here, or a class/copy this file does not list for it, still needs the captain's Slack id
(U7RP6HKUZ).
WHY THIS EXISTS: every campaign send used to require a human's Slack id as the approver, so anything an agent sends
on its own - the reply-ref class picker, any future unattended runner - was refused at the door even when the copy
was already approved. The captain (2026-11-03: 'users aren't in the dark ... no human reviews is the goal') had
Fable pre-approve classes instead, so the approval is a RULING + the exact template, not a live human click.
WHAT AN ENTRY PROVES, EXACTLY: that a Fable ruling exists, in writing, naming this class. It never claims the prose
is right - the prose is pinned by the gate's byte-exact copy tests and by the ruled copy pack named below. Every
send made through a ruling id is stamped in the verify ledger with approver_kind=fable-ruling, the ruling id, and
the template identity hash (scripts/credit_review/verify_ledger.py, audit-stamps), so an audit can tell a
captain-approved send from a ruled one without reading any log.
ADDING A CLASS IS A REVIEWED EDIT, and needs all of: (1) a written Fable ruling naming the class and the copy, in
the ruling owner's own record; (2) the copy itself landed in the gate with byte-exact tests; (3) a line here naming
the ruling id, the campaign and the exact gate copy tokens - never a wildcard. Remove the line to withdraw the
class. The tokens are the GATE's own COPY values (what the ledger's copy_ref records: reply-ref renders 'refq' for
--copy q, status-doc-received renders 'docrecvn' for --copy queued-neutral), not the --copy words a caller types.
SLOTS THE CAPTAIN NAMED ON 2026-11-03 (enabled / not yet enabled):
refund-confirmation  - ENABLED below (ruling fable-ruling-1103-d2/refund-confirm, gate campaign
refund-confirm, copy token 'refundconfirm'). d2's ruling writes the body; the EMAIL
SUBJECT ('Your refund is on its way (Muso)') is the one customer support staged for that
read (data/cs-systemic-c3/refund-confirmations-ready-1103.md) because the ruling names only
a body - d2 reads the rendered note before either send, so the subject is read too.
status-update        - the status copies that read as an update (status-team-review, status-doc-received /i and
R1, uvn-status) each end by telling the user we will message them again. That forward
promise is outside ruling 103's 'no dates, no promises, no money', so enabling them on a
ruling id needs its own ruling. They keep the captain-id path until then. This includes
the picker's OTHER approved ref, fable-copy-1030-r5/i (reply-refs gate_copy
'queued-neutral', campaign status-doc-received): r5 approved its prose, but 103 does not
cover its closing promise, so it is not listed here and the gate refuses it.
claim-status         - same shape (claimstatus ends with the same forward promise); not enabled here.
